summary.text: Steven Otis is a Democratic member of the New York State Assembly who has represented District 91 in Westchester County since 2013 and is running for re-election on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines.
A former mayor of Rye, he chairs the Assembly Science and Technology Committee.

paragraphs.text: Steven Otis earned a bachelor's degree from Hobart and William Smith Colleges, a master of public administration from New York University and a law degree from Hofstra University School of Law.
He worked as chief of staff to state Senator Suzi Oppenheimer and as legislative director to state Senator Jeremy Weinstein.
Otis served as mayor of the City of Rye for 12 years, from 1998 to 2009, and his official biography describes him as the longest-serving mayor in the city's history.
Otis serves the Sound Shore communities of Westchester County in the 91st Assembly District.
He chairs the Science and Technology Committee and is a member of the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Education, Environmental Conservation, and Ways and Means committees.

His official biography says he helped initiate the Water Infrastructure Improvement Act of 2015, a state grant program for municipal clean water projects, and that his 'Living Shorelines' legislation was signed into law in 2023.
It also credits him with advocating for digital inclusion programs and for emergency medical services reform, including a 2025 law requiring county EMS plans.
